sections.overview: This small enchytraeid annelid is specialized for life on temperate coastal glaciers of western North America.
sections.identification: It is an elongate annelid with a head pore, many sensory structures and abruptly curved setae.
sections.habitat: It is known from coastal glaciers from southern Alaska through British Columbia and Washington to Oregon.
sections.diet: Field observations report grazing on snow algae and other tiny organisms on snow and glacier meltwater.
sections.behavior: Worms rise toward the shaded snow surface in the evening and retreat below the surface during bright daytime conditions.
sections.reproduction: Tight bundles have been observed in melt pools and may be associated with reproduction, but their function has not been confirmed for this species.
sections.ecology: It completes its life cycle in glacier ice and snow close to freezing. Physiological experiments found that its energy-nucleotide levels rise when cooled.
sections.conservation: Its habitat is shrinking as glaciers retreat, and field counts at some North Cascade glaciers have declined; these local observations are not a global population assessment.
